n: As Samuel ages, he appoints his sons as judges to help him. Sadly, Samuel's household will repeat a problem that ruined Eli's.
His sons Joel and Abiah serve as judges in Beer-sheba, far to the south.
Samuel's sons do not follow his example. They chase money, take bribes, and twist justice — exactly what the law forbids judges to do.
All of Israel's elders come together to Samuel's home in Ramah for a serious meeting.

The elders point to Samuel's age and his sons' corruption and ask for a king “like all the nations.” Their concern is real, but their solution reveals a desire to be like everyone else rather than to trust God.
Samuel is displeased and likely hurt, but instead of reacting, he takes the matter to the Lord in prayer.
The Lord comforts Samuel: the people are not really rejecting him but rejecting God as their King. Still, God allows them their choice — He respects agency.
God notes this is not new: since leaving Egypt, Israel has repeatedly abandoned Him for other gods. Now they are treating Samuel the same way.
The Lord tells Samuel to grant the request, but first to warn them solemnly about what a king will demand from them.

f.g: the king's rights and ways — what life under a king will be like

n: Samuel faithfully repeats to the people everything the Lord said.
First warning: the king will draft your sons into his army and chariot corps, even to run ahead of his chariot as a display of royal power.
He will make officers of some and force others to plow his fields, harvest his crops, and make his weapons.
He will take your daughters to work in the palace as perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
He will seize the best fields, vineyards, and olive groves and give them to his officials. This happened later with King Ahab and Naboth's vineyard.
He will tax a tenth of your grain and wine to pay his court. The Lord asked a tenth for Himself; now a king will demand his own.
He will take your servants, your finest young men, and your donkeys for his own projects.
He will take a tenth of your flocks, and in the end you yourselves will be his servants. The people who were freed from Pharaoh will choose a new kind of bondage.
When you cry out because of the king you chose, the Lord will not answer you then. Choices have consequences that cannot always be undone.

f.w: the LORD will not hear you

n: Despite the warning, the people refuse to listen and insist on having a king.
They want to be like the other nations, with a king to judge them and lead them in battle. But the Lord had always fought Israel's battles for them.
Samuel reports everything back to the Lord.
The Lord tells Samuel to give them a king. Samuel sends everyone home while God prepares the next step.
